title: Did Jericho's Walls Really Fall?
notes: Dating is contested; the script presents Garstang, Kenyon and Wood as claims. Not-proven line is beat 12.

beats.text: Joshua six: Israel marches around Jericho for seven days, and the wall falls.
Jericho is Tell es-Sultan, a mound beside a spring in the Jordan Valley.
beats.say: Jericho is Tel es-sool-TAHN, a mound beside a spring in the Jordan Valley.

beats.text: In the nineteen thirties, John Garstang found collapsed, burned walls near fourteen hundred BC.
beats.say: In the nineteen thirties, John GAR-stang found collapsed, burned walls near fourteen hundred B C.
beats.label: GARSTANG: C. 1400 BC

beats.text: In the nineteen fifties, Kathleen Kenyon re-dug it and disagreed.
beats.say: In the nineteen fifties, Kathleen KEN-yon re-dug it and disagreed.

beats.text: Those walls, she said, were far older: about twenty-three hundred BC.
beats.say: Those walls, she said, were far older: about twenty-three hundred B C.

beats.text: Her date for the later city's burning: about fifteen fifty BC.
beats.say: Her date for the later city's burning: about fifteen fifty B C.

beats.text: In nineteen ninety, Bryant Wood argued pottery and scarabs fit fourteen hundred BC.
beats.say: In nineteen ninety, Bryant Wood argued pottery and SCARE-abs fit fourteen hundred B C.
beats.label: WOOD: C. 1400 BC

beats.text: But radiocarbon dates on burned grain lean toward Kenyon's earlier date.
Jericho sits roughly two hundred fifty metres below sea level, among the oldest cities known.
What's not proven: that these walls fell for Joshua. The dating stays contested.
Garstang, Kenyon, Wood: one mound, three verdicts.
beats.say: GAR-stang, KEN-yon, Wood: one mound, three verdicts.

beats.text: Did the walls fall, or were they long gone? What's your verdict?
